fact: The Access to Information Act was enacted on 20 July 2018 and is the law the Information Commission's November 2025 whitepaper reviews and proposes to amend.

The Information Commission, the oversight body under the Act, is reported to have been issuing orders, decisions and directives under Part VII s.63(1) since 2019, which information holders have ignored; no decision or figure of requests is given, so applied is not recorded.

TechHive Advisory states the Information Commission was created under the Access to Information Act, so that Act is in force (no date of the Act is given; dated to the article's publication, 2024-06-04).

TechHive Advisory states the Information Commission was created under the Access to Information Act, and the 2023 Data Protection Act designates it the data protection authority (dated to the article's publication, 2024-06-04).
Seychelles' Information Commission investigated an appeal under the Access to Information Act 2018 by Merleen Rassool against the Agriculture Department.
The Information Commission found the Agriculture Department in breach of sections 11(1), 12 and 21 of the Act and closed the case on 15 November 2024.
Seychelles' Information Commission issued a decision notice under the Access to Information Act 2018 in the appeal of Karen Domingue against the Seychelles Planning Authority.
The Information Commission found the Planning Authority non-compliant with sections 11 and 17 of the Act and ordered full access to the requested files within 5 days of its compliance letter.
The OECD Anti-Corruption and Integrity Outlook 2026 says the Access to Information Act No.4/2018 regulates every person's right to access information from a public body.

The OECD says the Information Commission is an independent body established under the Act, with a Chief Information Commissioner appointed for a fixed five-year term, and that it audited 19 institutions in 2023 with no fines applied.
The Constitutional Appointments Authority states the Chief Information Commissioner and two members were appointed under Section 37(1) of the Access to Information Act.

The Constitutional Appointments Authority reports President Ramkalawan presented instruments of appointment to Chief Information Commissioner Mumtaz Hasan (reappointed) and commissioners Egbert Rosalie and Peter Lalande.
